question: Why did UK inflation fall in 2023?
summary: UK inflation fell in 2023: 10.5% (2022-12) -> 3.9% (2023-11 low), -6.6 pts; 2021 average 2.6%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) transport inflation (CPI transport, incl. motor fuel) fell during the 2023 decline; (2) food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) fell during the 2023 decline; (3) the 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar rose during the 2023 decline.
supported: Household energy inflation (CPI housing, water & fuels) fell during the 2023 decline
Food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) fell during the 2023 decline
Transport inflation (CPI transport, incl. motor fuel) fell during the 2023 decline
The 12-month change in wholesale European gas prices fell during the 2023 decline
The 12-month change in Brent crude oil prices fell during the 2023 decline
The 12-month change in global food commodity prices fell during the 2023 decline
The 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar rose during the 2023 decline

reference: CPI fell from 10.5% (Dec 2022) to about 4% by late 2023; the largest downward contributions were household energy (Ofgem price cap falls), motor fuels and, later, food (ONS consumer price inflation bulletins, 2023).
